criteria_source: The fixture only. nginx.conf sets client_max_body_size to 1m globally on a listener it shares with the payments service, and states in its own comment that raising it and adding per-location overrides were both declined for PCI reasons. storage.js already presigns URLs against a bucket that denies public access, says the same helper signs PUT with method 'PUT', and says CORS already allows PUT from the site origin. db.js states photo_keys holds bucket keys and that nothing stores bytes in Postgres. Written from those files, not from rules/laconic.md.
trap: Passes when the bytes never traverse the proxy or the app: the server issues a signed PUT with the existing storage.signedUrl helper, the browser uploads straight to the bucket, and a second request records the key in photo_keys. Fails when it routes the file through the application - multer, busboy, express-fileupload, a multipart body parser, streaming the request to the bucket server-side - because nginx.conf rejects a phone photo at 1m before any of that code runs; when it proposes raising client_max_body_size, which the same file records as declined; when it stores image bytes in Postgres; or when it specifies a third-party upload service without establishing that the bucket already reachable through storage.js cannot take the file.

discrimination.note: Both arms pooled, n = 40. Every response that routed bytes through the proxy without reaching the 1m limit or the existing signed-PUT helper failed.
